title: Booking agency and the Monday "Concert in Jam" in Newark
summary: He booked stars like Dexter, Ben Webster, Miles Davis and Max Roach, drawing students on a Newark bar's off-night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Then I would -- eventually -- I think this is around '52 or something -- I opened a booking agent. I started booking bands and singers. Still gigging. I (inaudible) Albany, I used to book New York -- (inaudible) all up around Albany. And Joe Marsh had left Hamp. He come up with a small -- Anybody had a little band or something like that. And I got into -- I used to book some things in Newark every Monday night called Concert In Jam. And Dexter was in town, and I used to book Dexter and I used to book Ben Webster over there. I booked Miles Davis over there. Everybody. I had the same thing that they had at Birdland, I put in Newark called the Concert In Jam.
Where was the establishment?

It was on -- right in the heart of Newark, directly downtown. Like it was -- A guy had long bar with a band. They had a house band working there on the weekend. And it was one of the best little bands in Newark.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Good tenor player, good rhythm section. All I would do is just bring the stars over. I had Max Roach over there and Art Blakely, when I call the battle of the drums.
Art Blakey?
Art Blakey and Max Roach together on that.
Then I had -- what's the tenor player that used to play with Basie? Tall fella, played so good with Basie?
Buddy Tate?
Buddy Tate.
I had Buddy Tate and another tenor player. Then I had Ben Webster.
But see, Ben Webster wasn't supposed -- Ben Webster was the star. See I had called the battle of the tenors, see.
And Buddy Tate and another tenor player was battling. And then Ben Webster was supposed to come on at the end of it.
And I had two disc jockeys. I had a white disc jockey and a colored disc jockey. One would bring on the first part of the show. After intermission,

then Ben Webster would come on. Because I remember Ben Webster would stand back in the back -- he say, "When do I go?" I say, "You're gonna come on the end. You're the star," you know. I brought him on as a star. And after Buddy Tate and everybody got through playing, then we brought on Ben Webster. He did "Cotton Tail", and all (inaudible). Then they all wind up together. They'd get into this whole thing, you know, which was great. And Buddy and them -- they'd come out and jam the whole thing together. See, I didn't know that Rutgers University was in Newark at that time. But all the kids were coming over. And I wonder, "Where all these kids -- college kids are coming from?" And this was the school where they were coming from to catch the jazz stuff.
Yeah. I think it was called Newark College. It may have been called Newark State College.

Yeah, Newark State college -- something like that.
Yeah.
Because --
I think it's the engineering school what's called New Jersey Institute of Technology.
Yeah.
It may have had another name but they --
Yeah.
